newsitem.title: PERU: Strong blast rocks Peru electric firm - police.
newsitem.headline: Strong blast rocks Peru electric firm - police.

text.p: A powerful blast rocked an electric company early on Sunday on the outskirts of Lima, police said.

Local radio said the explosion at 6:15 a.m. local time (1115 GMT) at the building of Peruvian electricity generator Edelnor was an attack by leftist rebels. Police could not immediately confirm the report.
There was no immediate word of injuries.

"We have information about a powerful explosion in Canto Grande but we're awaiting word from our units," Lieutenent Franco Ruiz of the Peruvian police bomb squad UDEX said, referring to a poor district in eastern greater Lima.
Peru's two rebel groups, the Shining Path and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), have often bombed government and business installations in 16 years of rebel violence.
A group of 15 heavily armed MRTA guerrillas are currently holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. The hostage crisis is in its 54th day.
